result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend stacked cards with the same field order, keep the desktop table, and add a sticky search. B does better on rubric item 4: it labels date, total and tracking, keeps tracking on one line, and explains why it renders a separate card list (restyled table cells cause screen-reader problems). A puts date, total and ship method on one muted line with no labels, but it is stronger on making tracking tappable, since tapping the number opens the carrier's page. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend the same stacked-card layout, keep the desktop table and open with search, so they are close. A is better on item 4: every value keeps its label ('Placed', 'Total', 'Tracking'), and status is shown as a word, not by color alone. B squeezes date, total and ship method into one unlabeled muted line, though B is stronger on making the tracking number tappable to the carrier page and on weighing the two ways to build it.
